_comment: md5 of the REFERENCE dataset builds. ALL references are canonical under: numpy 2.4.1 + PYTHONHASHSEED=0 (build_from_manifest.py enforces the latter by re-exec). Upstream build_arc_dataset.py iterates a set of (split,subset) string tuples, so without a pinned hash seed the train/test SAVE order — and therefore the position of the train-split translational-pad RNG draws — flips on a per-process 50/50 coin, yielding exactly two internally-deterministic builds (identifiers and the entire test split are invariant between the two; only train/{inputs,labels}.npy differ). The ARC-2 test split is what the published-checkpoint eval reads, so K-numbers are identical either way. A build whose hashes differ from these is NOT comparable for training: see h010nf_voting_recompute.md (CLOSED section) for the cross-site incident, and the arc1/arc2 _comment fields for the coin-face history.
_comment_raw_data: Exact raw-data submodule commits the reference builds were made from. NOTE ConceptARC: this is NOT the commit pinned by HRM@ac15626 (b22ef52, Nov 2024) — upstream later fixed an erroneous output grid in corpus/Order/Order5.json (commit 0e67da6, 'Fixed error in demonstration 2 of Order5', Feb 2026; the ONLY content difference, and it is output-only). Our reference arc1 build uses the FIXED data; building from the HRM pin reproduces everything except train/all__labels.npy. build_from_manifest.py verifies these commits before building.

arc2._comment: Canonical = PYTHONHASHSEED=0 build (test-first save order), verified stable across two independent rebuilds 2026-06-11. The original Jun-2 reference happened to be built on the OTHER coin face (train-first): its train hashes were inputs 0d349adea46e8723a484c3ea7557cafc, labels ee38d067c3e435b8a22d8cf457049310. identifiers + the ENTIRE test split are identical between faces, so all published-checkpoint eval results (K=2=5.00% etc.) are unaffected. No in-house ARC-2 training has used either face's train split.

arc1._comment: Canonical = PYTHONHASHSEED=0 build = byte-identical to the ORIGINAL May-3 reference (test-first save order). History: a 2026-06-11 interim commit briefly re-baselined train/{inputs,labels} to the other coin face (inputs 9fa63c9cf6b12d6fdd91697ac723605c, labels a11e48a47db13a16e11f7f7770d42a7d) under a mistaken numpy-version theory; reverted same day once the hash-seed coin was identified and the =0 build reproduced the original hashes twice. numpy is exonerated: 2.4.1 reproduces everything given PYTHONHASHSEED=0. In-house baselines were trained on this canonical build.
